verdict.rationale: Honcho documents an MCP server that gives any MCP-compatible agent persistent memory, plus an API and SDK. Through these an agent can store messages, query context, and search or ask natural-language questions about memory mid-conversation. However, memory is mostly derived by background reasoning rather than written explicitly by the agent, and no evidence shows the agent updating or deleting memories itself. Missing for 10: agent-invoked update and delete operations, documentation of the actual MCP tool list for memory writes, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can manage its own memory mid-conversation — adding, searching, updating, and deleting memories through tools or API calls it invokes itself

citations.quote: The Honcho MCP server gives any MCP-compatible AI tool persistent memory and personalization.
Store messages and events, let Honcho reason in the background, then query peer representations, session context, search results, or natural-language insights from any model or framework.
Shape retrieval with search, token budgets, summaries, and peer scoping.
efficient enough to use at every turn
